significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a distinct linear attributed-belief representation causally controls reports and that, in conflicts, "attribution errors coincide with the truth direction leaking into the belief readout"—a form-(ii) mechanism augmented by a form-(iii) predictive coupling between measurable leakage and errors. It establishes both a cross-agent/proposition phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing expectations for false-belief conflicts beyond merely showing that belief is decodable; this connects the latent-truth representations studied by Burns et al. (2022) and Marks and Tegmark (2023) to behavioral attribution failures such as those measured by FANToM. The negative branch would informatively rule out this specific linear-separation-and-leakage account, although it would not rule out nonlinear or distributed belief representations, and the two branches are determinate. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on LLM beliefs would not earn this score; the increment comes from the specific independently steerable belief/truth decomposition and leakage-error coupling, though the core "direction + causal role + repair" shape remains close to the topic's default hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "lightweight monitor for detecting when a model is about to conflate what an agent believes with what is true," based on probe-measured truth leakage, making it ex ante rather than merely an explanation after an attribution error occurs. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction that greater truth leakage accompanies attribution errors could survive as a transferable relation, whereas the particular linear direction itself would only provide a procedure for finding a new model-specific object. The hypothesis asserts generalization "across propositions and agents" and speaks of LLMs broadly, so the monitor could serve model auditors or deployment gatekeepers, although the stated possibility that findings "may be model-specific" limits confidence in cross-family uptake. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: belief research alone supplies no monitor or advance warning, while this claim specifically hands downstream users an error predictor with an action window.
